absent: Numeric values and interrelations of optimized instruction size, address prefix size, call size, call opcode, redzone size and breakpoint opcode.
Layout, entry conditions and lifetime of the per-mapping trampoline and the predicate testing whether an address lies inside it.
Behavior of generic helpers for dispatching syscall uprobes, writing opcodes, copying from pages, initializing instructions and classifying breakpoint encodings.
Full definitions of architecture probe, task uprobe state, register file, decoded instruction and memory mapping structures beyond fields touched here.
Locking, lifetime and concurrency rules for breakpoint install and restore callers and for concurrent patch verification.
Constant for the uprobe trap number and delivery semantics of forced signals and reported negative error codes.
Preconditions and exact failure modes of shadow-stack push, pop and frame-update helpers beyond the fault cases shown.

findings.text: User stack argument block exchanged with the uprobe trampoline holds four machine words in order for saved AX, R11, CX and return address, used to restore and later update register state around handler execution.

Opcode write verification context pairs a base virtual address with an expectation selector distinguishing plain breakpoint, fully optimized sequence, and hybrid breakpoint plus optimized tail, consulted before allowing a patch.

Execute-out-of-line operation table provides up to four hooks for inline emulation, pre execution adjustment, post execution fixup and abort handling, each receiving the architecture probe descriptor and register state.

Dedicated system call acts as trampoline return path; it rejects callers whose instruction pointer is outside trampoline range, copies the four-word block from user stack, rewrites registers to present probed instruction context, validates shadow stack, invokes the generic uprobe handler, then either returns directly when the handler moved the stack or restores the trampoline frame and arranges system return.

Patch precondition check reads a full optimized-length window from the target page at the supplied base and accepts only when its leading bytes match the shape demanded by the context expectation, otherwise signaling rejection.

Optimization proceeds through ordered globally synchronized stages from trapped NOP to patched tail to published optimized entry, with failure rollback preserving trap on first byte and restoring NOP body while retaining any call bytes already visible to concurrent entrants.

Unoptimization reverses the sequence by first trapping entry, then restoring NOP body bytes, then publishing the original first byte with reference count handling that can reclaim the private page, each stage separated by cross-CPU synchronization.

Optimized replacement is built as a stack-pointer adjusting address computation prefix followed by a relative call whose target is the per-mapping trampoline start, delegated to the staged updater for publication; removal delegates to the staged reverse updater with the saved original bytes.
Breakpoint installation entry avoids rewriting an already optimized location when optimization remains allowed, otherwise installs a single breakpoint byte as registration.

Original instruction restoration entry unoptimizes first when the location is currently optimized and marked optimizable, warning once on failure, otherwise restores the saved first opcode byte as deregistration.

Global optimization path serializes against address-space changes by holding the memory map write lock across revalidation of breakpoint presence and the attempt to optimize, recording a permanent per-probe failure flag if the attempt fails.

Optimization eligibility requires 64-bit instruction decoding, an exact ten-byte NOP form with a specific five-byte leading prefix and NOP classification, plus enough remaining bytes in the page to avoid a cross-page update.
Alternate build configuration provides empty RIP-relative helpers and unconditionally declines optimization, indicating optimization support is compile-time gated.

Stack emulation derives operand width from current user mode rather than system call context and pushes a machine word by decrementing the user stack pointer after a successful user memory store; default pre handling only invokes RIP-relative compensation.

Default post execution fixup first applies RIP-relative compensation, then either adjusts the instruction pointer by the execute-out-of-line displacement or replaces a call return address and updates shadow-stack tracking, and records that single-step flag handling was consumed when status-flag fixup applies.

Conditional branch recognition and outcome testing cover the eight standard x86 condition families derived from overflow, carry, zero, sign and parity flags, returning true for non-conditional opcodes during execution.

Branch emulation advances past the instruction length, pushes a return address with shadow-stack coordination for calls, suppresses the displacement when the tested condition is false, and otherwise transfers to the computed target, reporting success for inline completion.
Push emulation sources the value from the register file at a precomputed offset, performs the same checked user stack push, and advances the instruction pointer by the decoded length only on success.

If inline call emulation fails due to an inaccessible stack, a mangled out-of-line form with cleared displacement is executed to force a fault with correct signal information; the rare case where another thread grew the stack meanwhile is detected post execution and requests instruction restart after unwinding the push.

Branch classification accepts NOPs, short and near unconditional jumps, relative calls and both short and two-byte conditional jumps after normalizing the latter to short form, rejects encodings with operand-size prefix or malformed two-byte form, and records opcode, length and displacement for later emulation.

Push classification accepts only single-byte register pushes and the extended-register form with a single specific REX prefix on 64-bit builds, mapping each opcode to the corresponding register file offset and rejecting longer or otherwise encoded forms.

Instruction analysis entry decodes the saved probe bytes in address-space mode, marks ten-byte NOPs as optimizable without further validation, otherwise delegates to generic validation, prefers branch then push emulation tables, and for remaining opcodes annotates return, jump, call and flag fixups plus RIP-relative analysis before selecting default handling.

Pre execution entry runs any registered pre hook, redirects execution to the reserved out-of-line area, saves trap number and single-step flag state while enabling single-stepping, and clears hardware block-step mode when active.

Any user memory access failure or shadow-stack mismatch on the trampoline return path forces an illegal-instruction signal against the caller and returns a generic failure indication rather than resuming.
Per-mapping optimization requires 64-bit user mode and an existing mapping for the target, acquires or reuses a trampoline mapping, and releases a newly created trampoline if patching fails.

Optimization presence probing safely copies the candidate window from remote address space with forced split handling and confirms both the optimized encoding shape and that its embedded call displacement lands inside the known trampoline range.
Architecture optimization coordinator is a no-op unless the probe remains eligible, otherwise performs locked revalidation and patching as described.
Early initialization pins the first trampoline mapping page to the architecture trampoline entry point.

Operation table wiring assigns default handling with pre, post and abort hooks, branch handling with emulation plus call-restart post hook, and push handling with emulation only, where default pre and abort hooks only perform RIP-relative compensation.
Relative call operation is identified by decimal opcode 232, short unconditional jump by 235, near unconditional jump by 233, and single-byte register push operations span decimal 80 to 87.
Operand-size prefix that disqualifies branch optimization is decimal 102, and the sole accepted REX prefix for extended push emulation is decimal 65.
